newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by conglomerates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, led by conglomerates.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up on Thursday on the back of highly capitalised blue chip conglomerates, brokers said.
The all share index closed 9.5 points up at 839.2. Blue chip conglomerates John Keells Holdings rose 15 rupees to 365, Hayleys 15 to 275, Aitken Spence 9.75 to 209.75.

"After John Keells Holdings turned in exceptional results to June mainly on income from plantation, food and tourism, investors are bullish about Hayleys and Aitken Spence," said a broker who declined to be identified.
"Since all the conglomerates are exposed more or less to the same areas, investors are bullish on Hayleys and Aitken Spence which are yet to release interim results," he added.
Turnover was 115.03 million rupees, led by 54,700 shares of Development Finance, 72,400 John Keells Holdings,
Foreign buying was worth 58.22 million rupees and selling, 47.5 million.
Brokers say the Colombo all share should continue to rise as more interim results come out.
